1. **The date-only path** (no time component) â my fix added `calendar.setLenient(false);`. This was the path that had the bug, where `new GregorianCalendar(year, month - 1, day)` was created in lenient mode (the default), causing invalid dates like `2022-14-30` (month 14) and `2022-12-33` (day 33) to be silently rolled over into valid `Date` objects.

2. **The date-with-time/timezone path** â already had `calendar.setLenient(false);` (line 249), which is why `testDateParseInvalidTime` already passed.

## Summary

The issue was in `ISO8601Utils.parse()` in `/testbed/gson/src/main/java/com/google/gson/internal/bind/util/ISO8601Utils.java`. When parsing a date-only string (no `T` time component and no timezone), the code created a `GregorianCalendar` in the default lenient mode. In lenient mode, the calendar silently "absorbs" out-of-range field values by rolling them over (e.g., month 14 becomes February of the next year, day 33 of December becomes January 2 of the next year).

The minimal fix adds `calendar.setLenient(false);` to the date-only code path, matching the behavior already present in the date-with-time/timezone code path. With `setLenient(false)`, out-of-range values cause an `IllegalArgumentException` to be thrown when `calendar.getTime()` is called, which is then caught and rethrown as a `ParseException` (as the PR's expected behavior suggests an exception should be thrown).

I verified:
- The reproduction case from the PR (`2022-14-30` and `2022-12-33`) now throws exceptions instead of producing rolled-over dates.
- Valid dates (including leap-year dates like `2020-02-29`, year boundaries, compact `yyyyMMdd` format, dates with time/timezone, and leap-second truncation) still parse correctly.
- Invalid dates (non-leap-year `2021-02-29`, `2022-04-31`, month `00`, day `00`) now correctly throw.
